items.question: When must pitot heating be selected to AUTO or ON?
items.explanation: Pitot heating must be AUTO or ON at indicated OAT of +4 °C or less.

items.question: When must pitot heating be selected to AUTO or OFF?
items.explanation: Pitot heating must be AUTO or OFF at indicated OAT of +5 °C or more.

items.question: Is flight into known icing conditions permitted?
options: Yes, if pitot heating is ON
No, unless cold weather kit installed
items.explanation: Flight into known icing conditions is prohibited.

items.question: Is flight into freezing rain or freezing fog permitted?
options: Yes, if pitot heat is ON
items.explanation: Flight into freezing rain and freezing fog is prohibited.

items.question: What is the maximum crosswind component for Category A operation?
items.explanation: Maximum cross wind component must not exceed 20 kt (10 m/s).

items.question: Is take-off with a tailwind component permitted?
items.explanation: Take-Off with tail wind component is prohibited.

items.question: Are aerobatic manoeuvres permitted?
items.explanation: Aerobatic manoeuvres are prohibited.

items.question: Are practice autorotative landings permitted?
items.explanation: Practice autorotative landings are prohibited.

items.question: During autorotation, may ENG MODE switches be selected from FLIGHT to IDLE?
options: Yes, if both engines are operating
items.explanation: During autorotation the ENG MODE switches must NOT be selected from FLIGHT to IDLE except in an emergency.

items.question: What is the maximum slope for nose-up take-off or landing?
items.explanation: Sloped take-off/landing nose up is limited to 10°.

items.question: What is the maximum slope for nose-down take-off or landing?
items.explanation: Sloped take-off/landing nose down is limited to 7°.

items.question: What is the maximum slope for left or right wing low take-off or landing?
items.explanation: Left wing low and right wing low are each limited to 10°.

items.question: What is the maximum baggage compartment load?
items.explanation: Maximum baggage compartment load is 250 kg (550 lb).

items.question: What is the maximum unit load in the baggage compartment?
items.explanation: Maximum unit load is 450 kg/m² (92 lb/sq.ft).

items.question: What is the maximum cargo height in the baggage compartment?
items.explanation: Cargo height must not exceed 600 mm (2 ft).

items.question: During AEO flight, torque is above 100% and the aircraft is accelerating through 105 KIAS. Which limitation is relevant?
options: This is allowed as long as the aircraft remains below VNE
AEO flight with TQ above 100% is limited to 90 KIAS
This is allowed for 10 seconds as a transient torque condition
The limitation only applies during OEI operation
items.explanation: The RFM states that maximum airspeed in AEO with TQ above 100% is 90 KIAS.

items.question: You are flying an IFR approach at 7000 ft. What is the maximum IFR approach airspeed according to the AW169 limitation?
items.explanation: Maximum IFR approach speed is 130 KIAS up to 5000 ft, then reduced by 2 kt per 1000 ft above 5000 ft. At 7000 ft: 130 - 4 = 126 KIAS.

items.question: In OEI flight, TQ is indicating 150%. How should this be interpreted?
options: It is within the OEI maximum continuous range
It is within the OEI 2.5 minute range
It is only permitted as a 10-second transient
It exceeds the maximum OEI 2.5 minute limitation
items.explanation: For OEI transmission torque, maximum continuous is 140%, the 2.5 minute range is 141-174%, and the 10-second transient limit is 192%.

items.question: A running landing is planned on a prepared grass surface. What is the maximum ground speed for the running landing?
items.explanation: On prepared grass surfaces, maximum taxi speed is 20 knots GS, maximum rolling take-off or running landing speed is 30 knots GS, and maximum emergency landing speed is 50 knots GS.
references: AW169 RFM Section 1 - Ground Speed Limitations (p.1-11)

items.question: During engine start, ITT briefly reaches 810 °C for approximately one second. Which statement is correct?
options: This exceeds the engine start limitation because 750 °C is an absolute maximum
This is within the transient start allowance, provided the transient does not exceed 2 seconds
This is within the AEO 30-minute take-off range
This is only permitted during OEI operation
items.explanation: For engine starting, maximum ITT is 750 °C, with a transient allowance up to 825 °C for 2 seconds.

items.question: Which types of operation is the rotorcraft certified for?
options: Day/Night VFR and IFR, Category A, and operations with >9 passenger seats
items.explanation: The rotorcraft is certified in Cat A and B and eligible for Day/Night VFR and IFR, Cat A operation, and operations with more than 9 passenger seats.

items.question: CAT A operations are approved under which conditions?
items.explanation: CAT A operations are approved under Day/Night conditions.

items.question: What visual conditions are required for CAT A Take-Off?
options: Visual references in FATO area and Take-Off distance
items.explanation: For CAT A Take-Off, external visual references must exist in the FATO area and in the Take-Off distance.

items.question: What visual conditions are required for CAT A Landing?
options: Visual reference in FATO area and balked landing distance
items.explanation: For CAT A Landing, external visual references must exist in the FATO area and in the balked landing distance.

items.question: What is the minimum flight crew for Day/Night VFR and IFR?
options: One pilot (unless otherwise required by operating rules)
One pilot for VFR, two for IFR
items.explanation: Minimum crew is one pilot, unless otherwise required by operating rules.

items.question: Is single pilot operation permitted from the left seat?
items.explanation: Single pilot operation is not permitted from the left seat.

items.question: If CAT A Take-Off or Landing is carried out from the left seat, what is the minimum crew?
items.explanation: When Take-Off or Landing is carried out from the left hand seat, minimum flight crew is two pilots.

items.question: What is the maximum number of occupants including crew for basic approved configurations?
items.explanation: The maximum number of occupants, including crew, shall not exceed 10 for basic approved configurations.

items.question: What must each occupant have?
items.explanation: Each occupant must have a seat with seat belt and shoulder harness.

items.question: What is the maximum gross weight for towing or taxi?
items.explanation: Maximum gross weight for towing or taxi is 4650 kg.

items.question: What is the maximum gross weight for CAT B Take-Off/Landing?
items.explanation: Maximum gross weight for CAT B Take-Off/Landing is 4600 kg.

items.question: What is the minimum flight/rotor running gross weight?
items.explanation: Minimum flight/rotor running gross weight is 3300 kg.

items.question: What electrical load does “75%” mean in CAT B WAT charts?
items.explanation: In CAT B WAT charts, 75% means an electrical load of 75% on each DC generator has been included.

items.question: What electrical load does “25%” mean in CAT B WAT charts?
items.explanation: In CAT B WAT charts, 25% means an electrical load of 25% on each DC generator has been included.

items.question: Is CAT B Take-Off and Landing with tail wind permitted?
items.explanation: CAT B Take-Off and Landing with tail wind is prohibited.

items.question: What electrical load does “75%” mean in CAT B WAT charts?
options: An electrical load of 75% on each DC generator
75% of total system load across all buses
items.explanation: In CAT B WAT charts, 75% means that an electrical load of 75% on each DC generator has been included.

items.question: What electrical load does “25%” mean in CAT B WAT charts?
options: An electrical load of 25% on each DC generator
25% of total system load across all buses
items.explanation: In CAT B WAT charts, 25% means that an electrical load of 25% on each DC generator has been included.

items.question: At what altitude can a safe vertical reject be carried out up to 15 ft for weight up to 4600 kg?
items.explanation: A safe vertical reject can always be carried out from HIGE up to 15 ft for weight up to 4600 kg.

items.question: At what altitude can a safe vertical reject be carried out up to 15 ft for weight in excess of 4600 kg up to 4800 kg?
items.explanation: A safe vertical reject can always be carried out from HIGE up to 15 ft for weight in excess of 4600 kg up to 4800 kg up to 5000 ft.

items.question: At what altitude can a safe vertical reject be carried out up to 10 ft for weight in excess of 4600 kg up to 4800 kg?
items.explanation: A safe vertical reject can always be carried out from HIGE up to 10 ft for weight in excess of 4600 kg up to 4800 kg up to 10,000 ft.

items.question: What is the maximum airspeed in AEO with torque above 100%?
items.explanation: Maximum airspeed in AEO with TQ above 100% is limited to 90 KIAS.

items.question: What is the maximum landing gear operation airspeed (Vlo) when either SB169-150 or landing gear P/N 6F3200F00413 (or subsequent) has been installed?
items.explanation: With SB169-150 or landing gear P/N 6F3200F00413 installed, maximum landing gear operation airspeed is 130 KIAS.

items.question: What is the maximum landing gear operation airspeed (Vlo) when neither SB169-150 nor landing gear P/N 6F3200F00413 (or subsequent) has been installed?
items.explanation: Without SB169-150 or landing gear P/N 6F3200F00413 installed, maximum landing gear operation airspeed is 80 KIAS.

items.question: What is the maximum landing gear extended airspeed (Vle)?
items.explanation: Maximum landing gear extended airspeed (Vle) is Vne - 8 KIAS.

items.question: What is the minimum airspeed for flight under IFR (Vmini)?
items.explanation: Minimum airspeed for flight under IFR (Vmini) is 50 KIAS.

items.question: What is the maximum airspeed for IFR approach?
options: 120 KIAS up to 3000 ft, then reduce 2 kts per 1000 ft
130 KIAS up to 5000 ft, then reduce 2 kts per 1000 ft
140 KIAS up to 4000 ft, then reduce 2 kts per 1000 ft
150 KIAS up to 6000 ft, then reduce 2 kts per 1000 ft
items.explanation: Maximum airspeed for IFR approach is 130 KIAS up to 5000 ft, then reduce 2 kts every 1000 ft.

items.question: What is the maximum airspeed with one autopilot failed?
items.explanation: Maximum airspeed with one AP failed is 120 KIAS.

items.question: What is the maximum airspeed for operation of windscreen wipers?
items.explanation: Maximum airspeed for operation of windscreen wipers is 140 KIAS.

items.question: What is the minimum airspeed in autorotation?
items.explanation: Minimum airspeed in autorotation is 50 KIAS.

items.question: What is the maximum airspeed with one door locked open?
items.explanation: Maximum airspeed with one door locked open is limited to 80 KIAS.

items.question: What is the maximum airspeed with both doors locked open?
items.explanation: Maximum airspeed with both doors locked open is limited to 100 KIAS.

items.question: What is the maximum airspeed for opening/closing a door in flight?
items.explanation: Maximum airspeed for opening/closing door in flight is limited to 80 KIAS.

items.question: What must be installed to open the cabin sliding door(s)?
options: KIT DOOR LOCK PASSENGER DOORS P/N 6F5213F00111
items.explanation: To open the cabin sliding doors, the KIT DOOR LOCK PASSENGER DOORS P/N 6F5213F00111 must be installed.

items.question: Who must carry out door opening/closing in flight?
options: A person trained for this task
items.explanation: Opening/closing of doors in flight must be carried out by a person trained for this task.

items.question: What must be taken into consideration when opening/closing doors in flight?
options: Effect of airspeed/windspeed on the door(s)
items.explanation: Due consideration must be given to the effect of airspeed/windspeed on the door(s).

items.question: What is the maximum taxi speed on paved surfaces?
items.explanation: Maximum taxi speed on paved surfaces is 40 knots GS.

items.question: On paved surfaces above 10 knots GS, what must the nose wheel condition be?
items.explanation: Above 10 knots GS on paved surfaces the nose wheel must be locked.

items.question: What is the maximum speed for rolling Take-Off or running landing on paved surfaces?
items.explanation: Maximum speed for rolling Take-Off or running landing on paved surfaces is 60 knots GS.

items.question: What is the maximum speed for emergency landing on paved surfaces?
items.explanation: Maximum emergency landing speed on paved surfaces is 60 knots GS.

items.question: What is the maximum taxi speed on prepared grass surfaces?
items.explanation: Maximum taxi speed on prepared grass surfaces is 20 knots GS.

items.question: On grass surfaces above 10 knots GS, what must the nose wheel condition be?
items.explanation: Above 10 knots GS on grass surfaces the nose wheel must be locked.

items.question: What is the maximum speed for rolling Take-Off or running landing on grass surfaces?
items.explanation: Maximum speed for rolling Take-Off or running landing on grass surfaces is 30 knots GS.

items.question: What is the maximum emergency landing speed on grass surfaces?
items.explanation: Maximum emergency landing speed on grass surfaces is 50 knots GS.

items.question: What is the maximum speed with PARK BRAKE ON during CAT A Take-Off and Landing?
items.explanation: Maximum speed with park brake on during CAT A Take-Off/Landing is 5 knots GS.

items.question: At which OAT must Pitot heating be set to AUTO or ON?
items.explanation: Pitot heating must be set to AUTO or ON for indicated OAT of +4 °C or less.

items.question: At which OAT must Pitot heating be set to AUTO or OFF?
items.explanation: Pitot heating must be set to AUTO or OFF for indicated OAT of +5 °C or more.

items.question: Is flight into known icing conditions permitted?
items.explanation: Flight into known icing conditions is prohibited.

items.question: Is flight into freezing rain and freezing fog permitted?
items.explanation: Flight into freezing rain and freezing fog is prohibited.

items.question: What is the maximum crosswind component for Category A operation?
items.explanation: Maximum crosswind component for Category A operation must not exceed 20 kts.

items.question: Is Take-Off with tail wind permitted in Category A operation?
items.explanation: Take-Off with tail wind component is prohibited in Category A operation.

items.question: Are aerobatic manoeuvres permitted?
items.explanation: Aerobatic manoeuvres are prohibited.

items.question: Are practice autorotative landings permitted?
items.explanation: Practice autorotative landings are prohibited.

items.question: During autorotation, can ENG MODE switches be moved from FLIGHT to IDLE?
items.explanation: During autorotation the ENG MODE switches must not be selected from FLIGHT to IDLE except in an emergency.

items.question: Is selection of ENG MODE to IDLE/OFF for training permitted?
items.explanation: Selection of ENG MODE switch to IDLE/OFF for training is prohibited.

items.question: What are the slope landing/takeoff limits?
options: Nose up 10°, Nose down 7°, Left wing low 10°, Right wing low 10°
Nose up 7°, Nose down 10°, Left wing low 7°, Right wing low 10°
Nose up 10°, Nose down 10°, Left wing low 7°, Right wing low 7°
items.explanation: Slope limits are: Nose up 10°, Nose down 7°, Left wing low 10°, Right wing low 10°.

items.question: What is the maximum baggage compartment load?
items.explanation: Maximum baggage compartment load is 250 kg (550 lb).

items.question: What must be installed for baggage compartment load to be allowed?
options: Net or approved means securing cargo
items.explanation: Load in baggage compartment is allowed provided that baggage liners are installed.

items.question: What is the maximum unit load in baggage compartment?
items.explanation: Maximum unit load in baggage compartment is 450 kg/m² (92 lb/sq.ft).

items.question: What is the maximum cargo height in baggage compartment?
items.explanation: Cargo height in baggage compartment must not exceed 600 mm (2 ft).

items.question: Is carriage of dangerous goods permitted in baggage compartment?
items.explanation: Carriage of dangerous goods in baggage compartment is prohibited.

items.question: If the Baggage Compartment Extension (P/N 6F2580F01111) is installed, is load allowed on the baggage cabin extension floor?
items.explanation: If the baggage compartment extension is installed, no load is allowed on the baggage cabin extension floor.

items.question: What is the maximum total weight of long objects protruding in the baggage extension area?
items.explanation: The total weight of long objects protruding in the baggage extension area must not exceed 50 kg (110 lbs).

items.question: Where must long objects be secured when placed in the baggage extension area?
items.explanation: Long objects must be secured to the main baggage floor.

items.question: Is cargo transport in the cabin permitted?
options: Only if an approved cabin configuration for cargo transport is installed
items.explanation: Cargo transport in the cabin is prohibited unless an approved cabin configuration is installed.
